parts.text:
I have this take home exam lets just do the setting up teh dontent project with latest dotnet version
we will use a clean archieture approach lets keep inital set up simple with simple here and use a clean archetiure for the app and just hello world dont implement teh actual features yet
additionally add swagger ui for easy dev use 
Lets use the dotnet skill to build out the inital setup for teh project

the exam breif
Benefits Engineering
Engineering candidate test for Benefits
This test is an opportunity to show how you translate a simple User Story into an elegant
RESTful API that enables your Squad’s Frontend Engineers to build products that will
delight our customers.
 Please use a .NET tech stack
 Do all your work in a new Git Repository - git init
 Commit your code in small working increments to show understanding.
 Aim for your solution is runnable and testable, please provide relevant
instructions.
 While it is a small, thin API, consider using any practices or opinions you’d
expect to see in a real service.
Please share a link to your GitHub repo and give the following users access:
 [REDACTED-reviewer]
 [REDACTED-reviewer]
 [REDACTED-reviewer]
 [REDACTED-reviewer]
 [REDACTED-reviewer]
Please spend no more than 180 minutes on your implementation.
As an HR Administrator
I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access
to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.
Acceptance criteria:
We must store: EmployeeNo, Title, Firstname, Surname, DOB, Gender, email,
Address
EmployeeNo must be generated and unique
Email must be unique
Assumptions:
Authentication is not important
How the data is stored is not important

Using AI?
If using AI extensively, please consider including a copy of your session export with the
submission.

The user wants a take-home exam project setup — Benefits Engineering, .NET with Clean Architecture containing just a hello world endpoint and Swagger. They mention "dotnet skill" (there's no dotnet skill in the list — closest is my own knowledge). Regarding whether I need to load a Postman API skill: this task involves no API design, mocking, testing, or deployment work — it's just scaffolding a hello-world solution, so I can proceed directly without loading `api-engineer`.

I'll check the dotnet and git/cliff setup.
I'll set up the initial Benefits API project with clean architecture. Let me check the environment first.

No dotnet skill in my available skills list. I'll just do it directly. Latest SDK is 10.0.300 — use net10.0. Init git repo, create solution with clean architecture layers:

- Benefits.Api (presentation, Web API with Swagger)
- Benefits.Application (use cases)
- Benefits.Domain (entities)
- Benefits.Infrastructure (persistence later)

Hello world endpoint + swagger. Commit in small increments as the brief says.

Let me create the git repo and solution. Note that working directory is the benefix folder which has .agents/.claude/skills-lock.json. Better to create the repo inside a subfolder, e.g., /Users/[REDACTED-user]/my_stuff/benefix/... hmm. The user said "the content project" — likely "the dotnet project." They said "we will use the dotnet skill" — there's no such skill available. I'll just proceed.

Where should the git repo go? The current dir isn't a git repo. Probably create the project in this folder directly? The .agents/.claude stuff is local tooling; the brief says "Do all your work in a new Git Repository - git init". I'd git init in the benefix folder but exclude tooling dirs in .gitignore. Or create a subfolder like Benefits.Api solution. I think creating solution files directly in this folder is fine, with .gitignore ignoring .agents/.claude/skills-lock.json. Actually cleaner: keep solution at root of this folder.

Let me scaffold:

dotnet new sln -n Benefits
dotnet new webapi -n Benefits.Api -o src/Benefits.Api
dotnet new classlib -n Benefits.Domain -o src/Benefits.Domain
dotnet new classlib -n Benefits.Application -o src/Benefits.Application
dotnet new classlib -n Benefits.Infrastructure -o src/Benefits.Infrastructure

Use net10.0. Add references, packages (Swashbuckle for net10 — dotnet new webapi in .NET 8 includes Swashbuckle; .NET 10 SDK template uses Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi with openapi.json and Scalar? Actually .NET 9 template uses Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi; .NET 10 template adds OpenAPI document generation built-in. The user asked for Swagger UI, so add Swashbuckle.AspNetCore package.

Keep it simple: minimal API or controllers? Clean architecture with a simple controller is fine. I'll use controllers, a HelloWorldController returning "Hello, World!" via Application layer service (thin but shows layering).

Commits in small increments:
1. git init + .gitignore
2. solution + projects skeleton
3. project references
4. hello world + swagger
5. README

Test project? "runnable and testable" — add a test project now? User said keep initial setup simple with just hello world. But a test project skeleton aligns with "testable". I could add Benefits.Api.Tests with one simple test. That's cheap and shows intent. Let me add one xUnit test project. Keep it small.

Let me do this step by step.

There's no dotnet skill installed in this session, so I'll scaffold it directly with the .NET 10 SDK (latest available here). Plan: git init, solution with clean architecture layers (Api / Application / Domain / Infrastructure), hello world endpoint + Swagger, plus a test project, committed in small increments.

# Benefits API

A thin RESTful API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test, built with .NET 10.

## Architecture

Clean Architecture, with the following layers:

| Project                          | Responsibility                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/Benefits.Domain`            | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                                       |
| `src/Benefits.Application`       | Use cases and application services (e.g. `IGreetingService`). Depends only on Domain.             |
| `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`    | Persistence and external concerns. Depends on Application.                                        |
| `src/Benefits.Api`               | ASP.NET Core REST API exposing Application use cases. Swagger/OpenAPI enabled in development.      |
| `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`       | Unit and integration tests (xUnit, in-memory `WebApplicationFactory`).                             |

Dependency rule: `Api -> Application -> Domain`, with `Infrastructure -> Application`.
The Domain has no outward dependencies.

## Getting started

```bash
dotnet restore
dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
```

- API: `https://localhost:xxxx` / `http://localhost:5182`
- Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)

## Hello World endpoints

- `GET /api/helloworld` -> `"Hello, World!"`

## Running tests

```bash
dotnet test
```

## Feature implementation

The target user story — adding a new starter (`EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`,
`Surname`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Email`, `Address` with generated unique `EmployeeNo`
and unique `Email`) — is not yet implemented; this repo currently contains the
scaffold and a hello-world endpoint only.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (and human contributors) working on the Benefits API.

## Project overview

A thin RESTful .NET 10 API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test.
The goal is to translate the user story below into an elegant RESTful API
that enables frontend engineers to build products that delight customers.
Authentication is not important. How the data is stored is not important
(but see **Storage** below for the chosen approach).

### User story

> As an HR Administrator
> I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access
> to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.

### Acceptance criteria

- We must store: `EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`,
  `Gender`, `Email`, `Address`
- `EmployeeNo` must be generated and unique
- `Email` must be unique

## Architecture (Clean Architecture)

| Project                         | Responsibility                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/Benefits.Domain`           | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                      |
| `src/Benefits.Application`      | Use cases / application services (e.g. `IGreetingService`). Depends on Domain only. |
| `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`   | Persistence and data access. Depends on Application.                             |
| `src/Benefits.Api`              | ASP.NET Core REST API. Controllers dispatch Application-layer use cases.          |
| `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`      | Unit and integration tests (xUnit).                                              |

Dependency rule: **`Api → Application → Domain`** and **`Infrastructure → Application`**.
The Domain depends on nothing the project. Nothing references `Benefits.Api`
except the test project (for its `Program` entry point).

- Controllers stay thin: bind request, call an Application use case, map response.
- Business rules (e.g. uniqueness validation, `EmployeeNo` generation) live in
  Domain or Application, never in controllers or SQL strings scattered around.

## Storage

- In-memory SQLite (`Data Source = :memory:`) to keep external dependencies
  small and the project runnable with zero infrastructure.
- Recommended data access: `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` + Dapper (small footprint,
  no ORM). EF Core (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`) is an acceptable
  alternative if richer query ergonomics are needed later.
- Uniqueness for `EmployeeNo` and `Email` is enforced at the database layer
  with unique indexes; unique-violation errors surface through the data layer.
- `EmployeeNo` is generated by the Application layer, not by SQLite defaults.
- Schema creation lives in `Benefits.Infrastructure`. No layer other than
  Infrastructure writes or knows raw SQL.

## Testing requirements (must-read)

Every feature and behavior must be covered by **both**:

1. **Unit tests** — Domain/Application logic in isolation, no web framework,
   no real I/O.
2. **Integration tests** — in-memory server via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`
   exercising real endpoints over HTTP, with the same in-memory SQLite setup
   the app uses.

Conventions:

-_tests live in `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests` in files named `*Tests.cs`
  (e.g. `GreetingServiceTests`, `HelloWorldEndpointTests`).
- Integration test data is isolated per test; never rely on execution order
  or shared mutable state between tests.
**`dotnet test` passing is the definition of done before any commit.**

## Development commands

```bash
dotnet restore
dotnet build
dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
dotnet test
```

- HTTP listener: `http://localhost:5182` (see `src/Benefits.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json`)
- Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
- Integration tests do not require the API to be running; they host it in memory.

## Conventions

- Commit in small working increments with concise messages describing the change.
- Keep package dependencies minimal; prefer BCL and the packages already present.
- `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings` are enabled project-wide; follow existing code style.
- Primary constructors on controllers/test classes where convenient (see existing code).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Benefits API pre-commit hook: secret scanning, format verification, build.
+# Enable after cloning with: git config core.hooksPath .githooks
+set -euo pipefail
+
+echo "==> pre-commit: scanning staged changes for secrets"
+if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged -v
+else
+    echo "gitleaks not found; falling back to basic pattern scan (install gitleaks for full coverage)" >&2
+    added=$(git diff --cached -U0 --no-color --diff-filter=ACM | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++' || true)
+    if [ -n "$added" ] && echo "$added" | grep -nIE \
+        'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}'; then
+        echo "Potential secret found in staged changes. Commit blocked." >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+
+echo "==> pre-commit: verifying formatting (dotnet format --verify-no-changes)"
+dotnet format --verify-no-changes --verbosity quiet
+
+echo "==> pre-commit: building solution"
+dotnet build --nologo --verbosity quiet
+
+echo "==> pre-commit: all checks passed"

 A thin RESTful .NET 10 API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test.
 The goal is to translate the user story below into an elegant RESTful API
 that enables frontend engineers to build products that delight customers.
 Authentication is not important. How the data is stored is not important
 (but see **Storage** below for the chosen approach).
 
 ### User story
 
 > As an HR Administrator
 > I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access
 > to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.
 
 ### Acceptance criteria
 
 - We must store: `EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`,
   `Gender`, `Email`, `Address`
 - `EmployeeNo` must be generated and unique
 - `Email` must be unique
 
 ## Architecture (Clean Architecture)
 
 | Project                         | Responsibility                                                                  |
 | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`           | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                      |
 | `src/Benefits.Application`      | Use cases / application services (e.g. `IGreetingService`). Depends on Domain only. |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`   | Persistence and data access. Depends on Application.                             |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`              | ASP.NET Core REST API. Controllers dispatch Application-layer use cases.          |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`      | Unit and integration tests (xUnit).                                              |
 
 Dependency rule: **`Api → Application → Domain`** and **`Infrastructure → Application`**.
 The Domain depends on nothing the project. Nothing references `Benefits.Api`
 except the test project (for its `Program` entry point).
 
 - Controllers stay thin: bind request, call an Application use case, map response.
 - Business rules (e.g. uniqueness validation, `EmployeeNo` generation) live in
   Domain or Application, never in controllers or SQL strings scattered around.
 
 ## Storage
 
 - In-memory SQLite (`Data Source = :memory:`) to keep external dependencies
   small and the project runnable with zero infrastructure.
 - Recommended data access: `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` + Dapper (small footprint,
   no ORM). EF Core (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`) is an acceptable
   alternative if richer query ergonomics are needed later.
 - Uniqueness for `EmployeeNo` and `Email` is enforced at the database layer
   with unique indexes; unique-violation errors surface through the data layer.
 - `EmployeeNo` is generated by the Application layer, not by SQLite defaults.
 - Schema creation lives in `Benefits.Infrastructure`. No layer other than
   Infrastructure writes or knows raw SQL.
 
 ## Testing requirements (must-read)
 
 Every feature and behavior must be covered by **both**:
 
 1. **Unit tests** — Domain/Application logic in isolation, no web framework,
    no real I/O.
 2. **Integration tests** — in-memory server via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`
    exercising real endpoints over HTTP, with the same in-memory SQLite setup
    the app uses.
 
 Conventions:
 
 -_tests live in `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests` in files named `*Tests.cs`
   (e.g. `GreetingServiceTests`, `HelloWorldEndpointTests`).
 - Integration test data is isolated per test; never rely on execution order
   or shared mutable state between tests.
 **`dotnet test` passing is the definition of done before any commit.**
 
+## Git pre-commit hooks
+
+A pre-commit hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` runs before every commit:
+
+1. **Secret scanning** — gitleaks over staged changes (install with `brew install gitleaks`
+   or your package manager); a basic regex fallback runs if gitleaks is absent.
+2. **Format verification** — `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` (fix with `dotnet format`).
+3. **Build** — `dotnet build` must succeed.
+
+Enable the hooks after a fresh clone (one time):
+
+```bash
+git config core.hooksPath .githooks
+```
+
+If a check fails, fix the issue and amend or re-stage; do not use `--no-verify`
+unless the reviewer has agreed there is a legitimate reason.
+
 ## Development commands
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet build
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 dotnet test
 ```
 
 - HTTP listener: `http://localhost:5182` (see `src/Benefits.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json`)
 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 - Integration tests do not require the API to be running; they host it in memory.
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Commit in small working increments with concise messages describing the change.
 - Keep package dependencies minimal; prefer BCL and the packages already present.
 - `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings` are enabled project-wide; follow existing code style.
 - Primary constructors on controllers/test classes where convenient (see existing code).

```bash
# Enable with: git config core.hooksPath .githooks

if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then

else

    if git diff --cached --diff-filter=ACM --name-only -z | xargs -0 grep -nIE \
```

# Benefits API

A thin RESTful API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test, built with .NET 10.

## Architecture

Clean Architecture, with the following layers:

| Project                          | Responsibility                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/Benefits.Domain`            | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                                       |
| `src/Benefits.Application`       | Use cases and application services (e.g. `IGreetingService`). Depends only on Domain.             |
| `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`    | Persistence and external concerns. Depends on Application.                                        |
| `src/Benefits.Api`               | ASP.NET Core REST API exposing Application use cases. Swagger/OpenAPI enabled in development.      |
| `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`       | Unit and integration tests (xUnit, in-memory `WebApplicationFactory`).                             |

Dependency rule: `Api -> Application -> Domain`, with `Infrastructure -> Application`.
The Domain has no outward dependencies.

```bash
dotnet restore
```

`Surname`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Email`, `Address` with generated unique `EmployeeNo`
and unique `Email`) — is not yet implemented; this repo currently contains the
scaffold and a hello-world endpoint only.

Pre-commit hooks are set up and verified:

- **`.githooks/pre-commit`** (shell + `core.hooksPath` config — the Husky skill's Node toolchain would have contradicted your minimal-deps constraint, so I used the .NET/SDK-native equivalent) runs three gates on every commit:
  1. **Secret scanning** — gitleaks (8.30.1, installed via brew) over staged changes, with a regex fallback (AWS keys / private keys / JWTs) if gitleaks is missing
  2. **Formatting** — `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`
  3. **Build** — `dotnet build`
- **Verified both paths**: the hook commit itself passed all checks; a staged fake `GITHUB_TOKEN` commit was **blocked** (invalid secret stayed out of history, HEAD unchanged). Noted: gitleaks allowlists AWS's documented example key `[REDACTED aws key]E`, and weak/password rules require entropy(regex) matches — genuine high-entropy credentials are caught.
- **AGENTS.md + README** now document the hook (setup command: `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, and a warning against `--no-verify`).

The hook commit is local only — tell me if you want it pushed.

Index: AGENTS.md
===================================================================
--- AGENTS.md	
+++ AGENTS.md	
@@ -1,111 +1,122 @@
 # AGENTS.md
 
 Guidance for AI coding agents (and human contributors) working on the Benefits API.
 
 ## Project overview
 
 A thin RESTful .NET 10 API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test.
 The goal is to translate the user story below into an elegant RESTful API
 that enables frontend engineers to build products that delight customers.
 Authentication is not important. How the data is stored is not important
 (but see **Storage** below for the chosen approach).
 
 ### User story
 
 > As an HR Administrator
 > I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access
 > to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.
 
 ### Acceptance criteria
 
 - We must store: `EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`,
   `Gender`, `Email`, `Address`
 - `EmployeeNo` must be generated and unique
 - `Email` must be unique
 
+### Additional decisions (2025-11-08)
+
+- `Email`, `Firstname` and `Surname` are required fields; the remaining fields
+  (`Title`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Address`) are nullable.
+- `EmployeeNo` is a generated GUID, not a sequential number.
+- `Email` must be a validly formatted email address.
+- `DOB` must not be in the future.
+- `Gender` is a domain enum (`Male`, `Female`, `Other`, `PreferNotToSay`),
+  serialized over the wire as spaced strings (e.g. "Prefer not to say").
+
 ## Architecture (Clean Architecture)
 
 | Project                         | Responsibility                                                                  |
 | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`           | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                      |
-| `src/Benefits.Application`      | Use cases / application services (e.g. `IGreetingService`). Depends on Domain only. |
+| `src/Benefits.Application`      | Use cases / application services (e.g. `IAddStarterService`). Depends on Domain only. |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`   | Persistence and data access. Depends on Application.                             |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`              | ASP.NET Core REST API. Controllers dispatch Application-layer use cases.          |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`      | Unit and integration tests (xUnit).                                              |
 
 Dependency rule: **`Api → Application → Domain`** and **`Infrastructure → Application`**.
 The Domain depends on nothing the project. Nothing references `Benefits.Api`
 except the test project (for its `Program` entry point).
 
 - Controllers stay thin: bind request, call an Application use case, map response.
-- Business rules (e.g. uniqueness validation, `EmployeeNo` generation) live in
-  Domain or Application, never in controllers or SQL strings scattered around.
+- Business rules (e.g. uniqueness validation, `EmployeeNo` generation, required
+  fields, date-of-birth sanity checks) live in Domain or Application, never in
+  controllers or SQL strings scattered around.
 
 ## Storage
 
 - In-memory SQLite (`Data Source = :memory:`) to keep external dependencies
   small and the project runnable with zero infrastructure.
 - Recommended data access: `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` + Dapper (small footprint,
   no ORM). EF Core (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`) is an acceptable
   alternative if richer query ergonomics are needed later.
 - Uniqueness for `EmployeeNo` and `Email` is enforced at the database layer
   with unique indexes; unique-violation errors surface through the data layer.
 - `EmployeeNo` is generated by the Application layer, not by SQLite defaults.
 - Schema creation lives in `Benefits.Infrastructure`. No layer other than
   Infrastructure writes or knows raw SQL.
 
 ## Testing requirements (must-read)
 
 Every feature and behavior must be covered by **both**:
 
 1. **Unit tests** — Domain/Application logic in isolation, no web framework,
    no real I/O.
 2. **Integration tests** — in-memory server via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`
    exercising real endpoints over HTTP, with the same in-memory SQLite setup
    the app uses.
 
 Conventions:
 
 -_tests live in `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests` in files named `*Tests.cs`
   (e.g. `GreetingServiceTests`, `HelloWorldEndpointTests`).
 - Integration test data is isolated per test; never rely on execution order
   or shared mutable state between tests.
 **`dotnet test` passing is the definition of done before any commit.**
 
 ## Git pre-commit hooks
 
 A pre-commit hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` runs before every commit:
 
 1. **Secret scanning** — gitleaks over staged changes (install with `brew install gitleaks`
    or your package manager); a basic regex fallback runs if gitleaks is absent.
 2. **Format verification** — `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` (fix with `dotnet format`).
 3. **Build** — `dotnet build` must succeed.
 
 Enable the hooks after a fresh clone (one time):
 
 ```bash
 git config core.hooksPath .githooks
 ```
 
 If a check fails, fix the issue and amend or re-stage; do not use `--no-verify`
 unless the reviewer has agreed there is a legitimate reason.
 
 ## Development commands
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet build
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 dotnet test
 ```

# Benefits API

A thin RESTful API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test, built with .NET 10.

## Architecture

Clean Architecture, with the following layers:

| Project                          | Responsibility                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/Benefits.Domain`            | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                                       |
| `src/Benefits.Application`       | Use cases and application services (e.g. `IGreetingService`). Depends only on Domain.             |
| `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`    | Persistence and external concerns. Depends on Application.                                        |
| `src/Benefits.Api`               | ASP.NET Core REST API exposing Application use cases. Swagger/OpenAPI enabled in development.      |
| `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`       | Unit and integration tests (xUnit, in-memory `WebApplicationFactory`).                             |

Dependency rule: `Api -> Application -> Domain`, with `Infrastructure -> Application`.
The Domain has no outward dependencies.

## Getting started

```bash
dotnet restore
dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
```

- API: `https://localhost:xxxx` / `http://localhost:5182`
- Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)

## Hello World endpoints

- `GET /api/helloworld` -> `"Hello, World!"`

## Running tests

```bash
dotnet test
```

## Git hooks

A pre-commit hook checks for leaked secrets (gitleaks), verifies formatting
(`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`) and builds the solution. Enable it once
after cloning:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

Secret scanning works best with [gitleaks](https://gitleaks.io) installed
(`brew install gitleaks`); a basic regex fallback runs if it is absent.

## Feature implementation

The target user story — adding a new starter (`EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`,
`Surname`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Email`, `Address` with generated unique `EmployeeNo`
and unique `Email`) — is not yet implemented; this repo currently contains the
scaffold and a hello-world endpoint only.

 # AGENTS.md
 
 Guidance for AI coding agents (and human contributors) working on the Benefits API.
 
 ## Project overview
 
 A thin RESTful .NET 10 API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test.
 The goal is to translate the user story below into an elegant RESTful API
 that enables frontend engineers to build products that delight customers.
 Authentication is not important. How the data is stored is not important
 (but see **Storage** below for the chosen approach).
 
 ### User story
 
 > As an HR Administrator
 > I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access
 > to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.
 
 ### Acceptance criteria
 
 - We must store: `EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`,
   `Gender`, `Email`, `Address`
 - `EmployeeNo` must be generated and unique
 - `Email` must be unique
 
 ### Additional decisions (2025-11-08)
 
 - `Email`, `Firstname` and `Surname` are required fields; the remaining fields
   (`Title`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Address`) are nullable.
 - `EmployeeNo` is a generated GUID, not a sequential number.
 - `Email` must be a validly formatted email address.
 - `DOB` must not be in the future.
-- `Gender` is a domain enum (`Male`, `Female`, `Other`, `PreferNotToSay`),
-  serialized over the wire as spaced strings (e.g. "Prefer not to say").
+- `Gender` is a domain enum (`Male`, `Female`, `Other`, `PreferNotToSay`).
+  Requests accept the member names (case-insensitive) or spaced forms
+  (e.g. "Prefer not to say"); responses serialize as spaced strings, and an
+  invalid value returns a 400 listing the allowed values
+  (`GenderParser` in Application, wire naming via `TitleCaseEnumNamingPolicy`).
 
 ## Architecture (Clean Architecture)
 
 | Project                         | Responsibility                                                                  |
 | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`           | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                      |
 | `src/Benefits.Application`      | Use cases / application services (e.g. `IAddStarterService`). Depends on Domain only. |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`   | Persistence and data access. Depends on Application.                             |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`              | ASP.NET Core REST API. Controllers dispatch Application-layer use cases.          |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`      | Unit and integration tests (xUnit).                                              |
 
 Dependency rule: **`Api → Application → Domain`** and **`Infrastructure → Application`**.
 The Domain depends on nothing the project. Nothing references `Benefits.Api`
 except the test project (for its `Program` entry point).
 
 - Controllers stay thin: bind request, call an Application use case, map response.
 - Business rules (e.g. uniqueness validation, `EmployeeNo` generation, required
   fields, date-of-birth sanity checks) live in Domain or Application, never in
   controllers or SQL strings scattered around.
 
 ## Storage
 
 - In-memory SQLite (`Data Source = :memory:`) to keep external dependencies
   small and the project runnable with zero infrastructure.
 - Recommended data access: `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` + Dapper (small footprint,
   no ORM). EF Core (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`) is an acceptable
   alternative if richer query ergonomics are needed later.
 - Uniqueness for `EmployeeNo` and `Email` is enforced at the database layer
   with unique indexes; unique-violation errors surface through the data layer.
 - `EmployeeNo` is generated by the Application layer, not by SQLite defaults.
 - Schema creation lives in `Benefits.Infrastructure`. No layer other than
   Infrastructure writes or knows raw SQL.
 
 ## Testing requirements (must-read)
 
 Every feature and behavior must be covered by **both**:
 
 1. **Unit tests** — Domain/Application logic in isolation, no web framework,
    no real I/O.
 2. **Integration tests** — in-memory server via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`
    exercising real endpoints over HTTP, with the same in-memory SQLite setup
    the app uses.
 
 Conventions:
 
 -_tests live in `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests` in files named `*Tests.cs`
   (e.g. `GreetingServiceTests`, `HelloWorldEndpointTests`).
 - Integration test data is isolated per test; never rely on execution order
   or shared mutable state between tests.
 **`dotnet test` passing is the definition of done before any commit.**
 
 ## Git pre-commit hooks
 
 A pre-commit hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` runs before every commit:
 
 1. **Secret scanning** — gitleaks over staged changes (install with `brew install gitleaks`
    or your package manager); a basic regex fallback runs if gitleaks is absent.
 2. **Format verification** — `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` (fix with `dotnet format`).
 3. **Build** — `dotnet build` must succeed.
 
 Enable the hooks after a fresh clone (one time):
 
 ```bash
 git config core.hooksPath .githooks
 ```
 
 If a check fails, fix the issue and amend or re-stage; do not use `--no-verify`
 unless the reviewer has agreed there is a legitimate reason.
 
 ## Development commands
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet build
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 dotnet test
 ```
 
 - HTTP listener: `http://localhost:5182` (see `src/Benefits.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json`)
 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 - Integration tests do not require the API to be running; they host it in memory.
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Commit in small working increments with concise messages describing the change.
 - Keep package dependencies minimal; prefer BCL and the packages already present.
 - `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings` are enabled project-wide; follow existing code style.
 - Primary constructors on controllers/test classes where convenient (see existing code).

 # Benefits API
 
 A thin RESTful API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test, built with .NET 10.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 Clean Architecture, with the following layers:
 
 | Project                          | Responsibility                                                                                    |
 | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`            | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                                       |
 | `src/Benefits.Application`       | Use cases and application services (e.g. `IAddStarterService`). Depends only on Domain.          |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`    | Persistence and external concerns. Depends on Application.                                        |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`               | ASP.NET Core REST API exposing Application use cases. Swagger/OpenAPI enabled in development.      |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`       | Unit and integration tests (xUnit, in-memory `WebApplicationFactory`).                             |
 
 Dependency rule: `Api -> Application -> Domain`, with `Infrastructure -> Application`.
 The Domain has no outward dependencies.
 
 ## Getting started
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 ```
 
 - API: `https://localhost:xxxx` / `http://localhost:5182`
 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 
 ## Endpoints
 
 - `POST /api/employees` — adds a new starter. See `src/Benefits.Api/Benefits.Api.http` for a sample request body.
 
 | Case                          | Status | Response                                   |
 | ----------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------ |
 | Starter saved                 | 200    | Saved employee (with GUID `employeeNo`)     |
 | Missing `email`/`firstname`/`surname` | 400 | ProblemDetails listing the missing fields |
 | Malformed `email`             | 400    | ProblemDetails                              |
 | `dob` in the future           | 400    | ProblemDetails                              |
-| Unknown `gender` value        | 400    | ValidationProblemDetails (Swagger shows allowed values) |
+| Unknown `gender` value        | 400    | ProblemDetails listing allowed values: `Male, Female, Other, Prefer not to say` |
 | `email` already registered    | 409    | ProblemDetails                              |
 
 Required fields: `email`, `firstname`, `surname`. All other fields are optional
 (`title`, `dob`, `gender`, `address`). `dob` must not be in the future.
+`gender` accepts the enum value names (case-insensitive) or their spaced
+forms, e.g. `"Male"`, `"prefer not to say"`.
 
 ## Running tests
 
 ```bash
 dotnet test
 ```
 
 ## Git hooks
 
 A pre-commit hook checks for leaked secrets (gitleaks), verifies formatting
 (`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`) and builds the solution. Enable it once
 after cloning:
 
 ```bash
 git config core.hooksPath .githooks
 ```
 
 Secret scanning works best with [gitleaks](https://gitleaks.io) installed
 (`brew install gitleaks`); a basic regex fallback runs if it is absent.
 
 ## Feature implementation
 
 Implements the user story: as an HR Administrator, add a new starter
 (`EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Email`,
 `Address`). `EmployeeNo` is a generated GUID (not sequential) and `Email`
 is unique; uniqueness is enforced by a unique index in the in-memory SQLite
 database and checked explicitly by the Application layer.

User wants a friendlier 400 response for invalid gender — one that lists the allowed enum values. Currently JSON parse failure surfaces the framework's generic ValidationProblemDetails with a cryptic converter message.

Options:
1. Accept string in the request DTO and map manually (custom validation) — this changes the model to `string? Gender` and then parse in Application or controller. This gives a fully custom, clear message like "Gender must be one of: Male, Female, Other, Prefer not to say." Wire response would then come from our own MissingRequiredFields-like error. But then EmployeeDto serialization should still output the spaced string.

2. Keep enum binding but customize the error via IModelErrorFactory / ApiBehaviorOptions InvalidModelStateResponseFactory in Program — customize the framework's 400 problem details to include allowed values. E.g., builder.Services.Configure<ApiBehaviorOptions>(o => o.InvalidModelStateResponseFactory = ...). We can produce a problem details message that enumerates allowed values when the error is on gender.

Option 1 is more explicit and puts validation in Application (per AGENTS.md: business rules in Domain/Application). Making AddStarterRequest.Gender a string and converting in the service has a downside: response DTO would need to echo as the string and the DTO's Gender typed enum... EmployeeDto still enum with converter for serialization. But request-side parse: service validates `request.Gender` string against enum names → descriptive error, new AddStarterError.InvalidGender.

Then invalid-gender becomes Application-level: status 400 from our own ProblemDetails with clear details listing allowed values — satisfying "make it more clear in the response that it should be one of the enum values."

But careful: JsonStringEnumConverter on serialization of response remains needed for the enum's wire name. Request DTO now has string Gender, so deserialize never hits converter for gender (string stays string). Response still uses naming policy. That decouples request handling from converter reading, making error messages precise. That's the cleanest approach and matches the earlier user pattern (they wanted Application validation for everything else).

Implementation:
- AddStarterRequest.Gender: `string?` (wire-exactly what client sends).
- Application: parse gender → allowed values with spaced names? The Application layer would need the same title-case naming logic... duplicating TitleCaseEnumNamingPolicy in Application. Hmm. The naming policy currently lives in Api. If Application validates gender strings "Male"/"Female"/"Other"/"Prefer not to say", it needs the wire-name logic → move TitleCaseEnumNamingPolicy to Application (shared), and Api uses it for JSON options. System.Text.Json ships in the shared framework for AspNetCore apps, but a plain classlib needs a package reference (System.Text.Json 10.x). That's a small dep. Acceptable.

The user is committing from their IDE (JetBrains) and the hook fails: `dotnet: command not found` and `gitleaks not found`. Why? GUI apps (JetBrains launched via Finder/Spotlight/Dock) don't inherit the shell PATH (`/usr/local/share/dotnet` and `/opt/homebrew/bin` aren't in PATH for GUI-spawned git).

Fix: make the hook robust — resolve dotnet/gitleaks via common install locations or PATH fallback:

```sh
for candidate in /usr/local/share/dotnet/dotnet /opt/homebrew/share/dotnet/dotnet "$HOME/.dotnet/dotnet"; do
```

Best approach: define PATH augmentation:

```bash
PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/share/dotnet:/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$HOME/.dotnet:$HOME/.cargo/bin:/usr/local/bin"
```

Then `command -v dotnet` works. gitleaks: /opt/homebrew/bin/gitleaks — covered by /opt/homebrew/bin addition.

Also capture: gitleaks not found earlier even though installed — same GUI PATH problem (brew is /opt/homebrew/bin which is missing).

Also locate DOTNET_ROOT: some apps need DOTNET_ROOT set for dotnet CLI; dotnet binary itself can locate SDK root relative to its own path — fine.

```bash
export PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/share/dotnet:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$HOME/.dotnet"
```

---

## Add starter service — `POST /api/employees`

### What this PR does

Implements the user story:

> As an HR Administrator, I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.

`POST /api/employees` accepts employee details and returns the saved employee with a generated `EmployeeNo`. Also removes the hello-world scaffolding endpoint now that the first real feature exists, and hardens the pre-commit hook's `PATH` so it works when git is invoked from GUI IDEs.

### Endpoint behaviour

| Case | Status | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starter saved | 200 | Saved employee (GUID `employeeNo` + echoed fields) |
| Missing `email` / `firstname` / `surname` | 400 | ProblemDetails **listing the exact missing fields** |
| Malformed `email` | 400 | ProblemDetails |
| `dob` in the future | 400 | ProblemDetails |
| Unknown `gender` | 400 | ProblemDetails **listing the allowed values** (`Male, Female, Other, Prefer not to say`) |
| `email` already registered | 409 | ProblemDetails |

### Reasoning & key decisions

**1. Clean Architecture, enforced by project references.** `Api → Application → Domain` and `Infrastructure → Application`; Domain has zero dependencies. Controllers only bind the request, call an Application use case, and map the result — business rules (uniqueness, email format, required fields, future-DOB check, GUID generation) live in Application/API composition layers, never in controllers or SQL.

**2. Result pattern instead of exceptions.** `AddStarterService` returns `AddStarterResult(Employee, Error, Message)` rather than throwing. Exceptions-as-control-flow for ordinary client errors (a duplicate email is *expected* traffic) is expensive and pushes validation semantics into exception handlers. The controller maps the typed error enum to status codes, so a 400 vs 409 decision is explicit rather than accidental.

**3. GUID `EmployeeNo`, generated in the Application layer.** A generated GUID satisfies "must be generated and unique" without a sequential-number system leaking business information (guessable IDs again later), and generating it in Application (not in the DB) keeps the ID known to the use case before persistence.

**4. Uniqueness is enforced twice.** The Application layer checks `EmailExistsAsync` first (fast, clean `409`), and the DB **unique index on `Email`** is the authoritative backstop — the repository maps the SQLite constraint-violation (`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT`) to `false`, so a race or a missed check still yields `409`, never a 500.

**5. In-memory SQLite + Dapper.** The brief says storage isn't important, so it's chosen to keep the dependency footprint minimal (`Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` + `Dapper` — no ORM) and the project runnable with zero infrastructure. The single connection is a registered singleton because SQLite drops an in-memory database when its last connection closes; no other layer sees raw SQL.

**6. Email validation via `System.Net.Mail`.** `MailAddress` parsing reflects the platform's own email parsing rather than a hand-rolled regex, so we don't write our own (necessarily incomplete) RFC 5322 subset.

**7. `Gender` as a domain enum with explicit wire handling.** The service accepts the enum's member names (case-insensitive) or their natural spaced forms (`"prefer not to say"`), and responses serialize via a small `TitleCaseEnumNamingPolicy`. Failed values get a **self-correcting 400 that enumerates the allowed values** instead of the framework's cryptic JSON-converter error. This required parsing `gender` as a string at the API boundary and validating in Application — worth calling out because the alternative (letting the JSON converter bind the enum) produced an opaque error message.

**8. Team decisions on required fields.** `Email`, `Firstname` and `Surname` are required (you can't be an employee without a name; uniqueness rules imply email is mandatory); `Title`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Address` are nullable. `DOB` must not be in the future — a sanity rule that surfaced naturally from the field's meaning. These are recorded in `AGENTS.md`.

**9. Descriptive structured logging.** Every save outcome logs with real values: `Starter saved successfully. EmployeeNo=…, Email=…, Name=…` (info) or `Starter not saved: an employee with email '…' already exists` (warn), so support can trace exactly what happened to a starter submission.

### Testing

21 xUnit tests, split (per `AGENTS.md`) between:

- **Unit** (14) — `AddStarterService` against an in-memory fake repository: save/echo, GUID generation and uniqueness across employees, each validation failure, case-insensitive gender parsing. No web framework, fast.
- **Integration** (7) — `WebApplicationFactory` hosting the real app with the real in-memory SQLite database, exercising genuine HTTP round-trips: 200 + payload shape, 409 duplicate, each 4XX, spaced-gender round-trip.

`dotnet test` green; `dotnet build` and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` clean; pre-commit ensures secrets/format/build per commit.

### What I'd do next

- `GET /api/employees/{employeeNo}` so the saved starter can be retrieved (frontend's first read)
- Return **201 Created + `Location`** header (this PR uses 200 per the brief's simplicity, already flagged)
- Repository-level integration tests for the SQLite edge behaviour (constraint mapping)

---

 # AGENTS.md
 
 Guidance for AI coding agents (and human contributors) working on the Benefits API.
 
 ## Project overview
 
 A thin RESTful .NET 10 API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test.
 The goal is to translate the user story below into an elegant RESTful API
 that enables frontend engineers to build products that delight customers.
 Authentication is not important. How the data is stored is not important
 (but see **Storage** below for the chosen approach).
 
 ### User story
 
 > As an HR Administrator
 > I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access
 > to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.
 
 ### Acceptance criteria
 
 - We must store: `EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`,
   `Gender`, `Email`, `Address`
 - `EmployeeNo` must be generated and unique
 - `Email` must be unique
 
 ### Additional decisions (2025-11-08)
 
 - `Email`, `Firstname` and `Surname` are required fields; the remaining fields
   (`Title`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Address`) are nullable.
 - `EmployeeNo` is a generated GUID, not a sequential number.
 - `Email` must be a validly formatted email address.
 - `DOB` must not be in the future.
 - `Gender` is a domain enum (`Male`, `Female`, `Other`, `PreferNotToSay`).
   Requests accept the member names (case-insensitive) or spaced forms
   (e.g. "Prefer not to say"); responses serialize as spaced strings, and an
   invalid value returns a 400 listing the allowed values
   (`GenderParser` in Application, wire naming via `TitleCaseEnumNamingPolicy`).
 
 ## Architecture (Clean Architecture)
 
 | Project                         | Responsibility                                                                  |
 | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`           | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                      |
 | `src/Benefits.Application`      | Use cases / application services (e.g. `IAddStarterService`). Depends on Domain only. |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`   | Persistence and data access. Depends on Application.                             |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`              | ASP.NET Core REST API. Controllers dispatch Application-layer use cases.          |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`      | Unit and integration tests (xUnit).                                              |
 
 Dependency rule: **`Api → Application → Domain`** and **`Infrastructure → Application`**.
 The Domain depends on nothing the project. Nothing references `Benefits.Api`
 except the test project (for its `Program` entry point).
 
 - Controllers stay thin: bind request, call an Application use case, map response.
 - Business rules (e.g. uniqueness validation, `EmployeeNo` generation, required
   fields, date-of-birth sanity checks) live in Domain or Application, never in
   controllers or SQL strings scattered around.
 
 ## Storage
 
 - In-memory SQLite (`Data Source = :memory:`) to keep external dependencies
   small and the project runnable with zero infrastructure.
 - Recommended data access: `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` + Dapper (small footprint,
   no ORM). EF Core (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`) is an acceptable
   alternative if richer query ergonomics are needed later.
 - Uniqueness for `EmployeeNo` and `Email` is enforced at the database layer
   with unique indexes; unique-violation errors surface through the data layer.
 - `EmployeeNo` is generated by the Application layer, not by SQLite defaults.
 - Schema creation lives in `Benefits.Infrastructure`. No layer other than
   Infrastructure writes or knows raw SQL.
 
 ## Testing requirements (must-read)
 
 Every feature and behavior must be covered by **both**:
 
 1. **Unit tests** — Domain/Application logic in isolation, no web framework,
    no real I/O.
 2. **Integration tests** — in-memory server via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`
    exercising real endpoints over HTTP, with the same in-memory SQLite setup
    the app uses.
 
 Conventions:
 
 -_tests live in `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests` in files named `*Tests.cs`
   (e.g. `GreetingServiceTests`, `HelloWorldEndpointTests`).
 - Integration test data is isolated per test; never rely on execution order
   or shared mutable state between tests.
 **`dotnet test` passing is the definition of done before any commit.**
 
 ## Git pre-commit hooks
 
 A pre-commit hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` runs before every commit:
 
 1. **Secret scanning** — gitleaks over staged changes (install with `brew install gitleaks`
    or your package manager); a basic regex fallback runs if gitleaks is absent.
 2. **Format verification** — `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` (fix with `dotnet format`).
 3. **Build** — `dotnet build` must succeed.
 
 Enable the hooks after a fresh clone (one time):
 
 ```bash
 git config core.hooksPath .githooks
 ```
 
 If a check fails, fix the issue and amend or re-stage; do not use `--no-verify`
 unless the reviewer has agreed there is a legitimate reason.
 
+CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same gates on every PR targeting
+`main`: restore/build/format-verify plus `dotnet test`, and a gitleaks secret
+scan. Both checks must pass before merge.
+
 ## Development commands
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet build
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 dotnet test
 ```
 
 - HTTP listener: `http://localhost:5182` (see `src/Benefits.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json`)
 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 - Integration tests do not require the API to be running; they host it in memory.
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Commit in small working increments with concise messages describing the change.
 - Keep package dependencies minimal; prefer BCL and the packages already present.
 - `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings` are enabled project-wide; follow existing code style.
 - Primary constructors on controllers/test classes where convenient (see existing code).

- **Triggers**: every PR → `main` and every push to `main`
- **Job 1 — "Build & test"**: restore → build → `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` → `dotnet test` (failures block the merge check)

Two setup notes for you:

(Can only be done in repo settings, not from the workflow.)
2. Commit/push is yours — once pushed, the workflow runs immediately on the push to your branch (push trigger is main-only, so it'll first execute when the PR is opened).

+FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
+WORKDIR /src
+
+# Corporate TLS interception (e.g. Cloudflare web gateway) breaks NuGet restore.
+# If a corporate root CA is supplied as a build secret, trust it; otherwise this
+# is a no-op and normal public CAs are used (CI, home networks, etc.).
+RUN --mount=type=secret,id=corp-root \
+    if [ -f /run/secrets/corp-root ]; then \
+        cp /run/secrets/corp-root /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-root.crt && \
+        update-ca-certificates; \
+        echo "Installed corporate root CA for build."; \
+    fi
+
+# Restore first with only project files present so dependency layers stay cached
+# across source-only changes.
+COPY src/Benefits.Domain/Benefits.Domain.csproj src/Benefits.Domain/
+COPY src/Benefits.Application/Benefits.Application.csproj src/Benefits.Application/
+COPY src/Benefits.Infrastructure/Benefits.Infrastructure.csproj src/Benefits.Infrastructure/
+COPY src/Benefits.Api/Benefits.Api.csproj src/Benefits.Api/
+
+RUN dotnet restore src/Benefits.Api/Benefits.Api.csproj
+
+COPY . .
+
+RUN dotnet publish src/Benefits.Api/Benefits.Api.csproj \
+    -c Release \
+    --no-restore \
+    -o /app/publish
+
+FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS runtime
+WORKDIR /app
+
+# 'app' (UID 1654) is the built-in non-root user of the .NET images.
+COPY --from=build --chown=app:app /app/publish .
+
+USER app
+
+EXPOSE 8080
+ENV ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080
+
+ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "Benefits.Api.dll"]

 # Benefits API
 
 [![CI](https://github.com/cderry95-cpu/benefix/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/cderry95-cpu/benefix/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
 
 A thin RESTful API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test, built with .NET 10.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 Clean Architecture, with the following layers:
 
 | Project                          | Responsibility                                                                                    |
 | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`            | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                                       |
 | `src/Benefits.Application`       | Use cases and application services (e.g. `IAddStarterService`). Depends only on Domain.          |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`    | Persistence and external concerns. Depends on Application.                                        |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`               | ASP.NET Core REST API exposing Application use cases. Swagger/OpenAPI enabled in development.      |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`       | Unit and integration tests (xUnit, in-memory `WebApplicationFactory`).                             |
 
 Dependency rule: `Api -> Application -> Domain`, with `Infrastructure -> Application`.
 The Domain has no outward dependencies.
 
 ## Getting started
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 ```
 
 - API: `https://localhost:xxxx` / `http://localhost:5182`
 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 
+### Docker
+
+```bash
+docker build -t benefix-api .
+docker run -p 8080:8080 benefix-api
+```
+
+- API listens on `http://localhost:8080`
+- Multi-stage build (SDK stage compiles, trimmed ASP.NET runtime stage runs it) running as a non-root user
+- Behind a corporate TLS-intercepting proxy (untrusted NuGet certificates in the build stage), pass a root CA PEM as a build secret:
+
+```bash
+docker build -t benefix-api --secret id=corp-root,src=<path-to-root-ca.pem> .
+```
+
 ## Endpoints
 
 - `POST /api/employees` — adds a new starter. See `src/Benefits.Api/Benefits.Api.http` for a sample request body.
 
 | Case                          | Status | Response                                   |
 | ----------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------ |
 | Starter saved                 | 200    | Saved employee (with GUID `employeeNo`)     |
 | Missing `email`/`firstname`/`surname` | 400 | ProblemDetails listing the missing fields |
 | Malformed `email`             | 400    | ProblemDetails                              |
 | `dob` in the future           | 400    | ProblemDetails                              |
 | Unknown `gender` value        | 400    | ProblemDetails listing allowed values: `Male, Female, Other, Prefer not to say` |
 | `email` already registered    | 409    | ProblemDetails                              |
 
 Required fields: `email`, `firstname`, `surname`. All other fields are optional
 (`title`, `dob`, `gender`, `address`). `dob` must not be in the future.
 `gender` accepts the enum value names (case-insensitive) or their spaced
 forms, e.g. `"Male"`, `"prefer not to say"`.
 
 ## Running tests
 
 ```bash
 dotnet test
 ```
 
 ## CI
 
 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push/PR targeting `main`:
 
 1. **Build & test** — restore, build, `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, `dotnet test`; the "Build & test" check must pass before a PR can merge.
 2. **Secret scan** — gitleaks over the full git history ("Secret scan" check).

 (`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`) and builds the solution. Enable it once

 (`EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Email`,
 `Address`). `EmployeeNo` is a generated GUID (not sequential) and `Email`
 is unique; uniqueness is enforced by a unique index in the in-memory SQLite
 database and checked explicitly by the Application layer.

Options: inherit host CA certs or disable TLS validation (bad). Check how the host does nuget — dotnet restore on host works (earlier). Host uses macOS trust store. In container (Linux CA), the corporate root isn't there.

Workarounds:
1. Extract the corporate root CA from macOS system trust and mount/during build add it. Where's the user's proxy? Check env vars: `https_proxy`? The host may have system proxy config. Check `security find-certificate` too deep. Simplest: run `dotnet nuget` with cert... We can build with `--network` default and pass `DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER`? no.

Better: identify root cert: curl -v https://api.nuget.org 2>&1 | grep issuer on host shows proxy? On host curl works (it trusts system). Check issuer chain: `echo | openssl s_client -connect api.nuget.org:443 -servername api.nuget.org 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -issuer`. That shows leaf; need full chain. Multi-stage build needs cert during build stage. One approach: use BuildKit secret or just extract on the fly in build via COPY? Also the CI (GitHub actions ubuntu) doesn't need it — certificates differ per machine.

Better approach: make the Dockerfile flexible: accept `NUGET_CERT_PATH`/optional build arg copying an optional CA bundle if present; keep default flow clean. Then locally build with the corporate cert extracted:

- Extract issuer root: find cert in macOS system keychain named "Gateway CA - Cloudflare Managed G2...". `security find-certificate -a -p -c "Gateway CA" /Library/Keychains/System.keychain > /tmp/corp-root.pem` (maybe -c search).

Then during build: `COPY corp-root.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` + `update-ca-certificates` (Debian images). To avoid committing corp cert, place it in a git-ignored file and use build arg/optional COPY with .dockerignore exceptions. COPY of missing file fails the build — so use optional build context trick: copy whole directory `certs/` if exists? COPY fails if source missing unless path exists (can COPY a dir that must exist). Trick: create empty dir + wildcard: `COPY certs/ /certs/` fails if no certs dir... `COPY cert* /` with no match errors. Standard pattern: use build arg `--build-arg`? COPY from arg not supported. Use `ONBUILD`? Hmm.

Alternative pass via named volume/mount at build? BuildKit `RUN --mount=type=secret` — secret mount for the PEM, then install to CA store if present. Requires BuildKit (docker 29 has it). Using secret keeps cert out of image and out of repo. In Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=corp-root \
    if [ -f /run/secrets/corp-root ]; then cp /run/secrets/corp-root /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-root.crt && update-ca-certificates; fi
```

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Corporate TLS interception (e.g. Cloudflare web gateway) breaks NuGet restore.
# If a corporate root CA is supplied as a build secret, trust it; otherwise this
# is a no-op and normal public CAs are used (CI, home networks, etc.).
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=corp-root \
    if [ -f /run/secrets/corp-root ]; then \
        cp /run/secrets/corp-root /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-root.crt && \
        update-ca-certificates; \
        echo "Installed corporate root CA for build."; \
    fi

# Restore first with only project files present so dependency layers stay cached
# across source-only changes.

 # AGENTS.md
 
 Guidance for AI coding agents (and human contributors) working on the Benefits API.
 
 ## Project overview
 
 A thin RESTful .NET 10 API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test.
 The goal is to translate the user story below into an elegant RESTful API
 that enables frontend engineers to build products that delight customers.
 Authentication is not important. How the data is stored is not important
 (but see **Storage** below for the chosen approach).
 
 ### User story
 
 > As an HR Administrator
 > I would like to be able to add a new starter so that they can gain access
 > to OneHub and take full advantage of their employment package.
 
 ### Acceptance criteria
 
 - We must store: `EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`,
   `Gender`, `Email`, `Address`
 - `EmployeeNo` must be generated and unique
 - `Email` must be unique
 
 ### Additional decisions (2025-11-08)
 
 - `Email`, `Firstname` and `Surname` are required fields; the remaining fields
   (`Title`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Address`) are nullable.
 - `EmployeeNo` is a generated GUID, not a sequential number.
 - `Email` must be a validly formatted email address.
 - `DOB` must not be in the future.
 - `Gender` is a domain enum (`Male`, `Female`, `Other`, `PreferNotToSay`).
   Requests accept the member names (case-insensitive) or spaced forms
   (e.g. "Prefer not to say"); responses serialize as spaced strings, and an
   invalid value returns a 400 listing the allowed values
   (`GenderParser` in Application, wire naming via `TitleCaseEnumNamingPolicy`).
+- `GET /api/employees` lists employees alphabetically by surname with offset
+  pagination (`page` default 1, `pageSize` default 10, max 100) and an
+  `{ items, page, pageSize, totalCount }` envelope.
+- In Development the API seeds 25 employees on startup when the table is
+  empty (`EmployeeDatabaseSeeder`); production never seeds. The in-memory
+  database resets per process, so dev restarts re-seed.
 
 ## Architecture (Clean Architecture)
 
 | Project                         | Responsibility                                                                  |
 | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`           | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                      |
 | `src/Benefits.Application`      | Use cases / application services (e.g. `IAddStarterService`). Depends on Domain only. |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`   | Persistence and data access. Depends on Application.                             |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`              | ASP.NET Core REST API. Controllers dispatch Application-layer use cases.          |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`      | Unit and integration tests (xUnit).                                              |
 
 Dependency rule: **`Api → Application → Domain`** and **`Infrastructure → Application`**.
 The Domain depends on nothing the project. Nothing references `Benefits.Api`
 except the test project (for its `Program` entry point).
 
 - Controllers stay thin: bind request, call an Application use case, map response.
 - Business rules (e.g. uniqueness validation, `EmployeeNo` generation, required
   fields, date-of-birth sanity checks) live in Domain or Application, never in
   controllers or SQL strings scattered around.
 
 ## Storage
 
 - In-memory SQLite (`Data Source = :memory:`) to keep external dependencies
   small and the project runnable with zero infrastructure.
 - Recommended data access: `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` + Dapper (small footprint,
   no ORM). EF Core (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite`) is an acceptable
   alternative if richer query ergonomics are needed later.
 - Uniqueness for `EmployeeNo` and `Email` is enforced at the database layer
   with unique indexes; unique-violation errors surface through the data layer.
 - `EmployeeNo` is generated by the Application layer, not by SQLite defaults.
 - Schema creation lives in `Benefits.Infrastructure`. No layer other than
   Infrastructure writes or knows raw SQL.
 
 ## Testing requirements (must-read)
 
 Every feature and behavior must be covered by **both**:
 
 1. **Unit tests** — Domain/Application logic in isolation, no web framework,
    no real I/O.
 2. **Integration tests** — in-memory server via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`
    exercising real endpoints over HTTP, with the same in-memory SQLite setup
    the app uses.
 
 Conventions:
 
 -_tests live in `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests` in files named `*Tests.cs`
   (e.g. `GreetingServiceTests`, `HelloWorldEndpointTests`).
 - Integration test data is isolated per test; never rely on execution order
   or shared mutable state between tests.
 **`dotnet test` passing is the definition of done before any commit.**
 
 ## Git pre-commit hooks
 
 A pre-commit hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` runs before every commit:
 
 1. **Secret scanning** — gitleaks over staged changes (install with `brew install gitleaks`
    or your package manager); a basic regex fallback runs if gitleaks is absent.
 2. **Format verification** — `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` (fix with `dotnet format`).
 3. **Build** — `dotnet build` must succeed.
 
 Enable the hooks after a fresh clone (one time):
 
 ```bash
 git config core.hooksPath .githooks
 ```
 
 If a check fails, fix the issue and amend or re-stage; do not use `--no-verify`
 unless the reviewer has agreed there is a legitimate reason.
 
 CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same gates on every PR targeting
 `main`: restore/build/format-verify plus `dotnet test`, and a gitleaks secret
 scan. Both checks must pass before merge.
 
 ## Development commands
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet build
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 dotnet test
 ```
 
 - HTTP listener: `http://localhost:5182` (see `src/Benefits.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json`)
 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 - Integration tests do not require the API to be running; they host it in memory.
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Commit in small working increments with concise messages describing the change.
 - Keep package dependencies minimal; prefer BCL and the packages already present.
 - `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings` are enabled project-wide; follow existing code style.
 - Primary constructors on controllers/test classes where convenient (see existing code).

+using Benefits.Domain;

+namespace Benefits.Infrastructure;

+/// <summary>
+/// Seeds a fixed set of development employees on startup so the API has data
+/// to list and page through in local development. No-op in production, and
+/// idempotent: it only inserts when the table is empty, so restarting or
+/// using the API never duplicates or overwrites real data.
+/// </summary>
+public sealed class EmployeeDatabaseSeeder(
+    EmployeeDatabase database,
+    IHostEnvironment environment,
+    ILogger<EmployeeDatabaseSeeder> logger) : IHostedService
+{
+    public Task StartAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) => SeedAsync(cancellationToken);
+
+    private async Task SeedAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
+    {
+        if (!environment.IsDevelopment())
+        {
+            logger.LogDebug("Employee seeding skipped: environment '{Environment}' is not Development.", environment.EnvironmentName);
+            return;
+        }
+
+        var existing = await database.Connection.ExecuteScalarAsync<int>(new CommandDefinition(
+            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employees",
+            cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
+
+        if (existing is not 0)
+        {
+            logger.LogInformation("Employee seeding skipped: {Count} employees already exist.", existing);
+            return;
+        }
+
+        foreach (var seed in SeedEmployees)
+        {
+            var employee = new Employee
+            {
+                EmployeeNo = Guid.NewGuid().ToString(),
+                Email = $"{seed.First}.{seed.Last}@example.test".ToLowerInvariant(),
+                Title = seed.Title,
+                Firstname = seed.First,
+                Surname = seed.Last,
+                Dob = new DateOnly(seed.Year, seed.Month, seed.Day),
+                Gender = seed.Gender,
+                Address = seed.Address,

All branches resolved. Shared understanding:
- Q1: GET /api/employees
- Q2: offset pagination page/pageSize
- Q3: no schema change; order alphabetically → Surname, Firstname, Email (my tie-break recommendation, user accepted "alphabetically")
- Q4: default page=1, pageSize=10; max 100; page>=1, pageSize>=1; invalid → 400 ProblemDetails; past-last-page → empty items with metadata
- Q5: seed 25 dev-only records, only if table empty; hosted service in Infrastructure; tests made deterministic
- Envelope: { items, page, pageSize, totalCount }

Plan of implementation:

**Application layer:**
- `Employees/ListEmployeesRequest.cs`? define query: page, pageSize as ints (retrieval from query string binding... binding happens in controller; Application defines ListEmployeesQuery(Page, PageSize)).
- Validation: ListEmployeesQuery validation in service (list employees) → error type. Reuse a new error enum: `ListEmployeesError`? Or validation result: invalid params → controller 400. Design: 
  - `PagedRequest`? Keep naming consistent with existing: `AddStarterRequest`. So `ListEmployeesRequest(Page, PageSize)` record with int? values? Controller binds from query `int? page, int? pageSize`. Validation:
  - Application `IListEmployeesService` with `ListEmployeesAsync(ListEmployeesRequest, ct)` returning `ListEmployeesResult` = `(IReadOnlyList<EmployeeDto> Items, int Page, int PageSize, int TotalCount)`; plus error cases for bad params. Options: result record + `ListEmployeesError` enum (`None`, `InvalidPagination` with message). Mirror AddStarter: `ListEmployeesResult(List? Items, Page, PageSize, TotalCount, Error, Message)`? Simpler: Records: 

```csharp
public sealed record ListEmployeesRequest(int? Page, int? PageSize);
public sealed record EmployeePage(IReadOnlyList<EmployeeDto> Items, int Page, int PageSize, int TotalCount);
public sealed record ListEmployeesResult(EmployeePage? Page, ListEmployeesError Error, string? Message = null);
```

Hmm naming: `EmployeePageDto`? Keep `ListEmployeesResult` with `Items/Page/PageSize/TotalCount` nullable + Error + Message. Simple:

```csharp
public sealed record ListEmployeesResult(
    IReadOnlyList<EmployeeDto>? Items,
    int Page,
    int PageSize,
    int TotalCount,
    ListEmployeesError Error = ListEmployeesError.None,
    string? Message = null)
```

Controller 400 if Error != None.

Validation rules in service:
- requestedPage = request.Page ?? 1; requestedPageSize = request.PageSize ?? 10.
- if requestedPage < 1 → error "page must be greater than or equal to 1."
- if requestedPageSize < 1 → error "pageSize must be greater than or equal to 1."
- if requestedPageSize > 100 → error "pageSize cannot exceed 100." 
Message can mention allowed range. Single InvalidPagination error covers.

- `IEmployeeRepository.ListAsync(int page, int pageSize, ct)` returning `(IReadOnlyList<Employee> Items, int TotalCount)`. Infrastructure: SQL:

```sql
SELECT EmployeeNo, ..., Address FROM Employees ORDER BY Surname, Firstname, Email LIMIT @Limit OFFSET @Offset
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employees
```

ExecuteAsync for items (query<Employee>) + ExecuteScalarAsync<int> for count. Surname can be NULL — SQLite ORDER BY: NULL sorts first ascending. Seeded + real rows have surname. Deterministic enough: NULL surname rows would lump together after? In SQLite ASC, NULLs first. Ties broken by Firstname/Email. Fine.

Dapper mapping: Employee record with required init props — Dapper maps by constructor? For records with init props Dapper uses the parameterized constructor when matched. public async Task<(IReadOnlyList<Employee> Items, int TotalCount)> ListAsync(int page, int pageSize, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
```csharp
{
    var offset = (page - 1) * pageSize;
    var items = (await database.Connection.QueryAsync<Employee>(new CommandDefinition(
        """
        SELECT EmployeeNo, Title, Firstname, Surname, Dob, Gender, Email, Address
        FROM Employees
        ORDER BY Surname, Firstname, Email
        LIMIT @PageSize OFFSET @Offset
        """,
        new { PageSize = pageSize, Offset = offset },
        cancellationToken: cancellationToken))).AsList();
    var totalCount = await database.Connection.ExecuteScalarAsync<int>(new CommandDefinition(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employees", cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
    return (items, totalCount);
}
```

Unexpected: after restart it seeded 25 again — count after restart is 25, log says "Seeded 25". That means the in-memory database did NOT persist — right, in-memory SQLite resets every process start. This is by design (Data Source=:memory: → fresh DB every run). So the "only when table empty" guard protects within a single process lifetime (e.g., hosted service could run once), and every dev restart re-seeds from scratch — 25 identical-shape records with fresh GUIDs. That's expected behavior worth documenting honestly (data resets per run in dev; fine since storage "not important").

Idempotency within process holds. The "skipped" path: can't trigger in dev via restart (fresh DB). It's still correct for the case where two hosted service instances... only one. So skip branch is effectively protective only if something else touched the table before the hosted service started (e.g. tests POSTing? No—seeder runs at startup before requests). It'll basically never fire in practice; harmless.

Document in README: dev DB resets on each run; seeder repopulates 25. Update README + AGENTS.md. Also .http GET sample. Let me finish docs.

Required fields: `email`, `firstname`, `surname`. All other fields are optional
(`title`, `dob`, `gender`, `address`). `dob` must not be in the future.
`gender` accepts the enum value names (case-insensitive) or their spaced
forms, e.g. `"Male"`, `"prefer not to say"`.

## Development seeding

When running locally (`Development` environment), the API seeds 25 realistic
