 A pre-commit hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` runs before every commit:
 
 1. **Secret scanning** — gitleaks over staged changes (install with `brew install gitleaks`
    or your package manager); a basic regex fallback runs if gitleaks is absent.
 2. **Format verification** — `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` (fix with `dotnet format`).
 3. **Build** — `dotnet build` must succeed.
 
 Enable the hooks after a fresh clone (one time):
 
 ```bash

 ```
 
 If a check fails, fix the issue and amend or re-stage; do not use `--no-verify`
 unless the reviewer has agreed there is a legitimate reason.
 
 CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same gates on every PR targeting
 `main`: restore/build/format-verify plus `dotnet test`, and a gitleaks secret
 scan. Both checks must pass before merge.

 ```bash

 dotnet build
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api

 ```

 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 - Integration tests do not require the API to be running; they host it in memory.

 - Keep package dependencies minimal; prefer BCL and the packages already present.

 # Benefits API
 
 [![CI](https://github.com/cderry95-cpu/benefix/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/cderry95-cpu/benefix/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
 
 A thin RESTful API for the Benefits Engineering take-home test, built with .NET 10.
 
+**For reviewers:** [`REVIEWERS.md`](REVIEWERS.md) documents the reasoning
+behind the design choices, what we deliberately deferred, and the questions
+we would have asked stakeholders.
+
 ## Architecture
 
 Clean Architecture, with the following layers:
 
 | Project                          | Responsibility                                                                                    |
 | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `src/Benefits.Domain`            | Domain entities and rules. No dependencies on other layers.                                       |
 | `src/Benefits.Application`       | Use cases and application services (e.g. `IAddStarterService`). Depends only on Domain.          |
 | `src/Benefits.Infrastructure`    | Persistence and external concerns. Depends on Application.                                        |
 | `src/Benefits.Api`               | ASP.NET Core REST API exposing Application use cases. Swagger/OpenAPI enabled in development.      |
 | `tests/Benefits.Api.Tests`       | Unit and integration tests (xUnit, in-memory `WebApplicationFactory`).                             |
 
 Dependency rule: `Api -> Application -> Domain`, with `Infrastructure -> Application`.
 The Domain has no outward dependencies.
 
 ## Getting started
 
 ```bash
 dotnet restore
 dotnet run --project src/Benefits.Api
 ```
 
 - API: `https://localhost:xxxx` / `http://localhost:5182`
 - Swagger UI: `/swagger` (development only)
 
 ### Docker
 
 ```bash
 docker build -t benefix-api .
 docker run -p 8080:8080 benefix-api
 ```
 
 - API listens on `http://localhost:8080`
 - Multi-stage build (SDK stage compiles, trimmed ASP.NET runtime stage runs it) running as a non-root user
 - Behind a corporate TLS-intercepting proxy (untrusted NuGet certificates in the build stage), pass a root CA PEM as a build secret:
 
 ```bash
 docker build -t benefix-api --secret id=corp-root,src=<path-to-root-ca.pem> .
 ```
 
 ## Endpoints
 
 - `GET /api/employees` — lists employees alphabetically by surname, paginated.
   Query params: `page` (default 1), `pageSize` (default 10, max 100). Response
   envelope: `{ items, page, pageSize, totalCount }`. A `page` beyond the end
   returns an empty `items` array with correct metadata; invalid params return
   a 400 ProblemDetails.
 - `GET /api/employees/{employeeNo}` — fetches a single employee by employee
   number; a 404 ProblemDetails is returned when no employee matches.
 - `DELETE /api/employees/{employeeNo}` — permanently deletes an employee;
   204 on success, 404 when the number is unknown (including already deleted).
 - `PUT /api/employees/{employeeNo}` — updates an employee's details (full
   replace: omitted nullable fields are cleared). The employee number can
   **not** be changed; the same validation as add applies (required
   email/firstname/surname, valid email, allowed gender values, no future DOB),
   and the updated employee is returned.
 - `POST /api/employees` — adds a new starter. See `src/Benefits.Api/Benefits.Api.http` for a sample request body.
 
 | Case                          | Status | Response                                   |
 | ----------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------ |
 | Employee updated              | 200    | Updated employee object (same employee number) |
 | Update targets unknown number | 404    | ProblemDetails ("Employee not found")      |
 | Employee deleted              | 204    | No content                                 |
 | Unknown employee number (GET/DELETE) | 404 | ProblemDetails ("Employee not found") |
 | Starter saved                 | 200    | Saved employee (with numeric `employeeNo`)  |
 | Employee looked up by number  | 200    | The employee object                        |
 | Missing `email`/`firstname`/`surname` | 400 | ProblemDetails listing the missing fields |
 | Malformed `email`             | 400    | ProblemDetails                              |
 | `dob` in the future           | 400    | ProblemDetails                              |
 | Unknown `gender` value        | 400    | ProblemDetails listing allowed values: `Male, Female, Other, Prefer not to say` |
 | `email` already registered    | 409    | ProblemDetails                              |
 
 Required fields: `email`, `firstname`, `surname`. All other fields are optional
 (`title`, `dob`, `gender`, `address`). `dob` must not be in the future.
 `gender` accepts the enum value names (case-insensitive) or their spaced
 forms, e.g. `"Male"`, `"prefer not to say"`.
 
 ## Development seeding
 
 When running locally (`Development` environment), the API seeds 25 realistic
 employees on startup if the table is empty, so pagination has real data to
 page through. Because the SQLite database is in memory, data resets on every
 restart and the seed runs again; production deployments never seed.
 
 ## Running tests
 
 ```bash
 dotnet test
 ```
 
 ## CI
 
 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push/PR targeting `main`:
 
 1. **Build & test** — restore, build, `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, `dotnet test`; the "Build & test" check must pass before a PR can merge.
 2. **Secret scan** — gitleaks over the full git history ("Secret scan" check).
 
 ## Git hooks
 
 A pre-commit hook checks for leaked secrets (gitleaks), verifies formatting
 (`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`) and builds the solution. Enable it once
 after cloning:
 
 ```bash
 git config core.hooksPath .githooks
 ```
 
 Secret scanning works best with [gitleaks](https://gitleaks.io) installed
 (`brew install gitleaks`); a basic regex fallback runs if it is absent.
 
 ## Feature implementation
 
 Implements the user story: as an HR Administrator, add a new starter
 (`EmployeeNo`, `Title`, `Firstname`, `Surname`, `DOB`, `Gender`, `Email`,
 `Address`). `EmployeeNo` is an integer of six random digits (e.g. `392573`) —
 human-readable and unique (existence-check retry
 backed by the database primary key), deliberately non-sequential so the
 number leaks nothing about headcount growth. `Email` is unique; uniqueness
 is enforced by a unique index in the in-memory SQLite database and checked
 explicitly by the Application layer.

+# Reviewer notes — reasoning and choices
+
+Candid notes on the decisions made during the implementation, what we would
+have done differently with more time, and the questions we would have taken
+to stakeholders. The short version of each feature's design is in
+[`README.md`](README.md); agent-facing conventions live in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).
+
+## Authentication and permissions (deliberately out of scope)
+
+The brief states that authentication is not important, so the API is open:
+there are no permission checks on who can add, view, update or delete an
+employee.
+
+With a login in place, this is what we would have added:
+
+- **Bearer-token authentication** storing the caller's identity on each
+  request.
+- **User groups / permission checks** so that:
+  - administrators can add, update and delete any employee;
+  - normal users can view **only their own** profile.
+- That would have materialised as a new `userType` column with an enum of
+  `Admin` / `Normal`, plus per-endpoint authorisation policies rather than
+  scattered role checks.
+- We would **not** have changed the data structure for this: the employee
+  table itself can stay exactly as it is, and the caller identity lives with
+  the authn/authz layer.
+
+If we were building the full login setup instead of open access, the natural
+choice would be **SSO** — we would ask stakeholders which providers to support
+(e.g. Microsoft Entra / Google / Okta). That offloads the risky parts (storing
+passwords, credential rotation, breach detection) to systems far more mature
+than anything sensible to build here. If self-hosted auth was required, we
+would at minimum add **2FA**.
+
+## Gender: why an enum
+
+Gender is a **fixed set of options**, so we modelled it as a domain enum
+(`Male`, `Female`, `Other`, `PreferNotToSay`) rather than a free-form string:
+
+- better for the **frontend**: the allowed values are enumerable
+  (the 400 response for an invalid value lists them, so clients can
+  self-correct);
+- better in the **DB**: stored as a typed value, not a string that can drift
+  (`"M"`, `"male"`, `"MALE"`, ...);
+- self-documenting in Swagger.
+
+## Employee number: readable integer vs GUID
+
+An additional GUID field would have made IDs even harder to deduce, but the
+choice was deliberately made that `EmployeeNo` should be an **easily
+human-readable id** — an integer of six random digits. It is **not
+sequential** on purpose, so it does not leak how many employees exist or how
+fast the company is growing, and uniqueness is still guaranteed by the
+database primary key plus the generator's collision-retry loop.
+
+## What we would ask stakeholders about
+
+The user story leaves several field-level truths open; with stakeholder
+access we would refine:
+
+- **Address**: do we want structured data (street lines, city, **postcode**)?
+  Is it a required field? Today it is an optional free-text field.
+- **First/last names**: we assumed they are required — logically an employee
+  number needs a name to identify the human. Would stakeholders want
+  **min/max length constraints** on them, and how do we treat hyphenated or
+  non-Latin names?
+
+## Nice-to-haves (deferred deliberately)
+
+- **Redis caching** for quicker reads (`GET` single/list), with write
+  operations (add/update/delete) invalidating or updating the affected cache
+  entry so reads never go stale.
+- Filtering/search on the list endpoint (surname/email) once the read path
+  is proven.
+- `201 Created` + `Location` header on POST rather than 200.

# Reviewer notes — reasoning and choices

Intro: candid notes on decisions made during the 180-minute exercise: what we'd do differently with more time, what we'd ask stakeholders.

## Authentication & permissions (deliberately out of scope)
The brief says auth not important, so the API is open. With login in place we would have:
- Bearer-token–authenticated requests storing the caller's identity.
- Role checks based on user groups/direction: admins can add/delete/update/view anyone; normal users only their own profile. This means a `userType` column (enum: Admin/Normal) + authorization middleware/policy per endpoint.

## Gender enum
Fixed options — chose a domain enum over strings: safer frontend consumption (allowed values, no typos "M", "male"...), better DB typing/lookup, self-documenting API error listing allowed values.

## Employee number: readable integer vs GUID
We considered adding a secondary GUID field for a less-deducible ID; chosen: six random (non-sequential) digits kept it human-readable — deliberate trade-off; uniqueness enforced with DB PK + retry. Not sequential by design.

- Address: structure (street lines? postcode?), required vs optional.
- Names: min/max length constraints on first/last; formatting.
- Anything else: employee exists before start date? etc. — don't invent much beyond user's stated list.

## Nice to haves (with more time)

# Intro

OpenCode is an open source coding agent. It’s available as a terminal-based interface, desktop app, or web app.


## CLI

<CodeTabs
  id="install"
  label="Install method"
  tabs={[
    { label: "curl", code: "curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash" },
    { label: "homebrew", code: "brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2" },
    { label: "npm", code: "npm install -g @opencode/cli" },
    { label: "bun", code: "bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli" },
    { label: "pnpm", code: "pnpm add -g --allow-build=@opencode/cli @opencode/cli" },
    { label: "yarn", code: "yarn global add @opencode/cli" },
    { label: "vite+", code: "vp install -g @opencode/cli" },
    { label: "aur", code: "paru -S opencode-beta" },
    { label: "mise", code: "mise use -g opencode" },
  ]}
/>

The npm package uses a postinstall script to select the native `opencode` binary for your platform. The Bun and pnpm commands
explicitly allow the required script; Vite+ requires no additional flag. The mise command requires mise 2026.10.9 or later;
older versions install OpenCode 1.

Windows package managers are not supported.


Download a standalone CLI binary for your platform.

- **macOS:** [Apple silicon](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-darwin-arm64.zip) · [Intel](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-darwin-x64.zip) · [Intel (baseline)](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-darwin-x64-baseline.zip)
- **Windows:** [ARM64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-windows-arm64.zip) · [x64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-windows-x64.zip) · [x64 (baseline)](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-windows-x64-baseline.zip)
- **Linux (glibc):** [ARM64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-linux-arm64.tar.gz) · [x64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz) · [x64 (baseline)](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-linux-x64-baseline.tar.gz)
- **Linux (musl):** [ARM64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-linux-arm64-musl.tar.gz) · [x64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-linux-x64-musl.tar.gz) · [x64 (baseline)](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/opencode/opencode-linux-x64-baseline-musl.tar.gz)

## Desktop

Download the latest OpenCode Desktop build for your platform.

- **macOS:** [Apple silicon](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Intel](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-mac-x64.dmg)
- **Windows:** [x64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-win-x64.exe) · [ARM64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-win-arm64.exe)
- **Linux (.deb):** [x64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-linux-amd64.deb) · [ARM64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-linux-arm64.deb)
- **Linux (.rpm):** [x64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-linux-x86_64.rpm) · [ARM64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-linux-aarch64.rpm)
- **Linux (AppImage):** [x64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-linux-x86_64.AppImage) · [ARM64](https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/opencode-desktop-linux-arm64.AppImage)


## Web

Access the OpenCode web interface with the `opencode pair` command.

```bash
$ opencode pair

  Open a link to connect. Links work once and expire in 5 minutes.

  http://127.0.0.1:49374/auth/connect/...
```

## Docker

Docker images use versioned tags, for example `ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:2.0.0`.

---

## Connect

OpenCode has built-in support for many LLM providers. You can connect to them
directly [in the TUI](/cli/providers) with `/connect`.

See [Providers](/providers) to configure custom providers.

If you'd like easy access to the best coding models, you can try out
[OpenCode Console](/console).

You can also try [OpenCode Go](/console/go), a $10/month subscription
plan that grants you access to the best coding models.

---

## Customize

Make OpenCode your own by editing the [OpenCode config](/config), [loading plugins](/plugins), [connecting MCP
servers](/mcp-servers), or [creating commands](/commands). For terminal interface themes and keybindings, see [CLI
settings](/cli/config).

---

## Learn

If you are interested in an in-depth course on OpenCode, Boot.dev has created an excellent [AI Coding with
OpenCode](https://www.boot.dev/courses/learn-ai-coding) course in consultation with our team. All the information in the course is
free to read and watch, though some interactive features may require payment.
